text:
1,058 third-grade students in Tuscarawas County schools in 2024-25 school year
There were 1,058 third-grade students enrolled in Tuscarawas County schools in the 2024-25 school year, 1.8% more than the previous year, according to reports from the Ohio Department of Education & Workforce.
South Elementary School welcomed the largest portion of third-grade students in the county, registering 206 students.
Within Tuscarawas County schools, 10th grade had the highest enrollment, while pre-kindergarten had the lowest.
Statewide, Tuscarawas County ranked 25th in enrollment numbers, with a total of 13,820 students enrolled in the 2024-25 school year. It was also ranked 25th the year before.
Public school enrollment in Ohio fell to 1.47 million students in fiscal year 2025, down 1%, marking the largest drop since fiscal year 2022.
According to a report from the Ohio Legislative Service Commission, enrollment fell most sharply in rural and small-town districts. In contrast, joint vocational districts recorded growth, with chartered nonpublic schools recording the largest enrollment increases.
According to an analysis by the Thomas B. Fordham Institute, Ohio students have not fully recovered from pandemic-related learning losses. In the 2024-25 school year, about 55.3% of students were proficient in math and 60% in reading, both several points below 2018-19 levels.
Ohio ranks 21st nationally in K-12 expenditures, with public schools spending $17,257 per pupil. Overall, K-12 education spending accounts for 3.54% of taxpayer income in the state, above the national average.
